dedupe_keys.name: traffic a python toolbox for processing and analysing air traffic data

description: traffic is a Python library that helps to work with common sources of air traffic data. Its main purpose is to provide data analysis methods commonly applied to aircraft trajectories and airspaces, with direct access to the underlying pandas data frames when a method is missing. It parses and accesses open ADS-B sources such as the OpenSky Network and Eurocontrol DDR files and is designed to be extended to other sources. Static visualisation uses Matplotlib and Cartopy, interactive work runs in Jupyter with ipyleaflet and altair, and exports reach CesiumJS and Google Earth. It is described in a paper in the Journal of Open Source Software. Coverage is whatever the data source covers, worldwide. Access: free on PyPI and conda-forge under the MIT licence; version 2.13 was uploaded on 22 July 2025 and needs Python 3.10 or later, with installation instructions in the documentation. Caveats: access to the OpenSky history needs an account granted by OpenSky, and results inherit gaps in receiver coverage. The library supports trajectory processing for airspace capacity, network flow and resilience studies of air transport. It complements the OpenSky Network, pyModeS and OpenAP catalogued here.
